::: {.callout-warning title="Preliminary, conditional estimates"}

This report estimates expected population counts. It does not identify missed
individual cases or give a distribution for the unknown realised count.
Numerical validation does not validate the external-data assumptions.

:::

## What the model estimates

For a cell with true DS probability $q$, recording sensitivity $s$, and
false-positive probability $f$, the recorded probability is

$$
P(R=1)=qs+(1-q)f.
$$

The count likelihood is Binomial with the observed cell birth count as its
denominator. Cells retain their age, year and certificate version where the
model uses those distinctions.

| Models | Prevalence or reduction | Recording |
|---|---|---|
| DSP001, DSP002 | Seven-band age risk and yearly reduction priors | Constant or centred year offsets |
| DSP003 | Exact-age risk and a smooth age reduction curve calibrated to each national margin | Constant |
| DSP004, DSP005 | Exact-age risk and yearly reduction priors | Constant or centred year offsets |
| DSP006 | Exact-age risk and yearly reduction priors | Separate revised and unrevised levels |
| DSP007, DSP008 | Annual prevalence anchored to surveillance windows | Constant or revision-specific |
| DSP009 | Surveillance-anchored prevalence | Revision-specific, with post-anchor drift |
| DSP010 | Surveillance-anchored prevalence | Revision-specific, with an anomaly-panel factor |

The age curve, false-positive rate, external observation model and recording
assumptions constrain the allocation between prevalence and recording. Birth
certificates alone do not identify that allocation.

## Expected counts

Each draw of the expected total is $\sum_c N_c q_c$. Its posterior interval
describes uncertainty in expected burden. It excludes the additional uncertainty
needed to infer the unknown realised count in these particular births.

The saved names true_count_year and true_count_total remain compatibility
aliases. New outputs also use expected_ds_count_year and expected_ds_count_total.

## Prior and posterior distributions

These tables use prior draws from the fitted model when available. An anchored
fit does not use the reduction-rate CSV as a prior. Any retained columns named
rho_external_reference describe an unused comparison series.

Older anchored artefacts may lack valid prior draws. Their prior columns are
left blank rather than filled from a different model. New anchored fits use
rejection sampling to include the probability-barrier term in their prior.
The proposal count and acceptance rate are stored in the manifest.

```{python}
#| echo: false
reduction = pd.read_csv("tables/core_reduction_prior_posterior.csv")
columns = [
    "year", "rho_prior_mean", "rho_prior_centre", "rho_prior_lo", "rho_prior_hi",
    "rho_prior_source", "rho_year_mean", "rho_year_lo", "rho_year_hi",
]
display(reduction[[column for column in columns if column in reduction]].round(4))
```

![Reduction prior and posterior where available](plots/core_reduction_prior_posterior.png)

For DSP001–DSP006, yearly logit reduction priors can include correlated errors
and a common calibration shift. Their extrapolated tail remains an assumption.
For DSP003, the age-curve solver preserves the sampled national margin using
weights $N_{y,a}\theta_a$. Fit validation checks its numerical error.

For DSP007–DSP010, the prior is instead an annual log-prevalence process.
Surveillance data constrain weighted window means through a joint Normal
observation model on the log scale.

## Surveillance observation assumptions

The starting log prevalence has a Normal prior with a fixed median of 0.0013
and log-scale SD of 0.25. The option --anchor-level-prior-prevalence changes the
median. This prior no longer takes its centre from the first observation.
The choice is a working prior and should be varied in sensitivity checks.

The default CLI uses annual birth counts to weight the pooled surveillance
prevalence. The weights cover every year in each observed window, including
years outside the fitted range. Missing weights are an error.

The observation covariance is an explicit working assumption. With window
design matrix $W$, the correlation is the standardised form of $WW^\mathsf{T}$.
This represents shared annual errors of equal variance. It does not establish
the true covariance of the surveillance programmes or capture every shared bias.

Use --anchor-overlap-share 0 for independent errors, intermediate values for
partial overlap, and --anchor-non-overlapping for a subset with no reused
years. Compare observation SD values as well. The option
--anchor-window-weighting equal_years reproduces the older equal-year mean.

```{python}
#| echo: false
anchor = config.get("surveillance_anchor")
if anchor:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{
        "weighting": anchor.get("window_weighting", "unverified_legacy"),
        "windows": anchor.get("n_windows"),
        **anchor.get("hyperpriors", {}),
    }]))
```

## Recording sensitivity

The recording_s parameter is the global centre, or the revised-certificate
reference level. It is not generally the overall sensitivity across all years
and certificate versions. Annual prior intervals include the fitted drift or
panel structure.

```{python}
#| echo: false
display(pd.read_csv("tables/core_recording_s.csv").round(4))
display(pd.read_csv("tables/core_recording_s_by_year.csv").round(4))
```

![Recording sensitivity by year](plots/core_recording_s_by_year.png)

For DSP009, the post-anchor walk divides changes between prevalence and
recording through its prior scale. A zero drift scale and a flat prevalence
forecast are useful allocation comparisons, not evidence that either is true.

For DSP010, a loading of one shares changes in log odds, not proportional
changes in sensitivity. With baseline sensitivity 0.34, a panel factor of 0.9
gives a sensitivity ratio of about 0.932. A common true-prevalence trend is not
identified by the controls alone, although the joint DS likelihood can update it.

The fixed panel-walk scale still applies shrinkage. Condition-specific trends
have an estimated scale and no exact sum-to-zero constraint. The common trend
and the mean condition trend remain partly confounded. The descriptive
heterogeneity calculation omits some sources of within-condition uncertainty,
which can inflate Q and I-squared.

## Predictive checks

A fit to totals does not establish a fit across ages or years. Inspect the joint
age-year checks where available, including sparse ages. The endpoint labels
10–12 and 50+ denote capped groups, not literal single ages.

```{python}
#| echo: false
for stem in (
    "core_ppc_by_year", "core_ppc_by_age", "core_ppc_by_age_band",
    "core_ppc_by_age_year", "core_reduction_by_age_year",
):
    table = Path("tables") / f"{stem}.csv"
    plot = Path("plots") / f"{stem}.png"
    if table.is_file():
        display(Markdown("### " + stem.replace("core_", "").replace("_", " ")))
        display(pd.read_csv(table).round(3))
    if plot.is_file():
        display(Image(filename=str(plot)))
```

## Validation and provenance

The validation.json file checks all free parameters, important reported
quantities, R-hat, bulk and tail effective sample sizes, divergences, energy
behaviour, probability overshoot and the age-calibration margin. Constant
deterministic quantities are explicitly exempted from undefined convergence
diagnostics. Tree-depth limits are reported separately as an efficiency warning.

A failed fit retains its diagnostics but returns a non-zero CLI status.
The manifest.json file records the code revision and source hashes, dependency
versions, actual sampler, input and cell-table fingerprints, prior-sampling
method and validation status. Older artefacts without this information are
unvalidated.

These checks do not establish correct identification, transportability of the
external age curve, missingness assumptions or surveillance accuracy. Revised
anchor likelihoods require refitting. Do not combine old and new fits as if
their observation models were unchanged.
